newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Millwall set for squad clear-out.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Millwall set for squad clear-out.

text.p: Millwall soccer club will retain John Docherty as manager but expects several changes among its playing staff as it aims for a promotion push next season, incoming chairman Theo Paphitis said on Friday.
"We need to maintain a squad capable of putting us back in the first division," Paphitis told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said that the second division club has more than 40 players on its books and that some of these would be sold to cut costs and generate revenue for new signings.
Paphitis is to take over as chairman of parent company Millwall Holdings Plc as part of a restructuring designed to guarantee the club's future.
The club is aiming to raise 10 million stg through a share placing and rights issue, using 7.25 million to pay off debts and the rest as working capital.
Paphitis said that only a small amount of that 2.75 million stg capital would be available to buy players. Any other deals would have to be financed from sales.

The new board wants to use the club's New Den stadium to host a number of other events such as concerts to increase revenue. "We've got a 20 million pound asset and it's only being used for 48 hours a year," Paphitis said.
The stadium's location in an unfashionable part of south London has been seen as a handicap but Paphitis said that events targeted at a young audience could be successful.
Paphitis said that he would and associated companies would be investing one million stg in the club. He said he had no worries about joining a club with a fearsome past reputation for fan violence.
"Anything that happens at Millwall is always big news. There are far worse problems with fans at other clubs."
